answer: Notary-witnessed binding: whether the operator lives by a lagoon or downtown, they visit a licensed notary who checks a government ID in person, signs a statement tying that ID's hash to the agent's key, and stamps a commission number the registry can look up. The registry rejects any ID hash already bound, so bots named Falcon and Juniper run by one person cannot both pass; each extra identity needs another real person, visit and ~$20 fee. Limit: a bribed notary or forged ID can slip through, so a notary whose stamps appear on caught fakes is struck off.
